questions.stem:
Statements: All pens are pencils. All pencils are scales.
Conclusions:
I. All pens are scales.
II. Some scales are pens.

options.option_text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: C is correct. Chain: pens ⊆ pencils ⊆ scales. I: All pens are scales (transitive chain) = TRUE. II: Some scales are pens (since all pens are scales, at least those pens are scales, making some scales = pens) = TRUE. Both follow.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some doctors are teachers. All teachers are engineers.
Conclusions:
I. Some doctors are engineers.
II. All engineers are teachers.

options.option_text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: A is correct. Some doctors → teachers (subset); all teachers → engineers. Those 'some doctors' who are teachers are also engineers → Some doctors are engineers (I = TRUE). II says all engineers are teachers — illegal conversion of 'all teachers are engineers'; engineering is a larger set. I follows, II does not.

questions.stem:
Statements: No bird is a fish. All fish are reptiles.
Conclusions:
I. No bird is a reptile.
II. Some reptiles are not birds.

options.option_text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: B is correct. No bird is a fish; all fish ⊆ reptiles. Those fish-reptiles are not birds → some reptiles are not birds (II = TRUE). For I: we only know birds and fish are separate; birds might still overlap with reptiles. I cannot be confirmed. Only II follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: All roses are flowers. Some flowers are petals.
Conclusions:
I. Some roses are petals.
II. Some petals are flowers.

options.option_text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: B is correct. All roses ⊆ flowers; some flowers ∩ petals ≠ ∅. Conclusion II: if some flowers are petals, then some petals are flowers (valid conversion of 'some' statement) = TRUE. Conclusion I: the petal-flowers might not include roses; we can't confirm roses overlap with petals. Only II follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are horses.
Conclusions:
I. All cats are horses.
II. No horse is a cat.

options.option_text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: A is correct. Chain: cats ⊆ dogs ⊆ horses. I: All cats are horses = TRUE by transitivity. II: 'No horse is a cat' = FALSE — since all cats are horses, some horses ARE cats. Only I follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some politicians are honest. Some honest people are brave.
Conclusions:
I. Some politicians are brave.
II. All brave people are honest.

options.option_text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: D is correct. Some+Some rule: no definite conclusion. The 'some honest politicians' and 'some honest brave' might not overlap. I cannot be confirmed. II says all brave are honest — direct illegal conversion of 'some honest are brave'. Neither conclusion follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: All lights are fans. Some fans are coolers.
Conclusions:
I. Some lights are coolers.
II. All coolers are fans.

options.option_text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: D is correct. All lights ⊆ fans; some fans ∩ coolers ≠ ∅. I: the fan-coolers might not include lights (lights are a subset of fans, but the cooler subset may not intersect with lights). I is uncertain. II: illegal reversal of 'some fans are coolers' → not all coolers need to be fans. Neither follows definitively.

questions.stem:
Statements: No river is an ocean. All oceans are seas.
Conclusions:
I. No river is a sea.
II. Some seas are not rivers.

options.option_text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: B is correct. Rivers and oceans are disjoint. All oceans ⊆ seas. Those ocean-seas are not rivers → some seas (the oceans) are not rivers (II = TRUE). I says no river is a sea — but seas include oceans AND possibly more; rivers might overlap with non-ocean seas. I is uncertain. Only II follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: All mangoes are sweet. No sweet thing is sour.
Conclusions:
I. No mango is sour.
II. All sweet things are mangoes.

options.option_text: Both conclusions I and II follow

questions.explanation: A is correct. Mangoes ⊆ sweet things; sweet things ∩ sour things = ∅. Since mangoes ⊆ sweet things and no sweet thing is sour → no mango is sour (I = TRUE). II reverses the first statement illegally; not all sweet things need to be mangoes. Only I follows.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some bikes are cars. All cars are trucks.
Conclusions:
I. Some bikes are trucks.
II. Some trucks are bikes.
III. All trucks are cars.
questions.explanation: A is correct. Some bikes → cars; all cars ⊆ trucks. Those bike-cars are also trucks → Some bikes are trucks (I = TRUE). Since some bikes are trucks → some trucks are bikes (valid conversion; II = TRUE). III says all trucks are cars — illegal reversal; not all trucks need to be cars. Only I and II follow.
